_comment: In a static method, `super.m()` looks `m` up on the parent class itself (not its prototype) and calls it with the current class as `this`: the parent's static method returns the service stored on the derived class. Under the class rule (a service that reaches class code bails its key; class code is every class body that is not a key class, and every function nested in one) the service reaches the static methods, so every method stays, including the unread one, and the bundle runs.
